static_traits.name: Lin Rui
static_traits.social_status: Has a best friend Cayden, can confide when encountering difficulties usually, but has not yet communicated with anyone about this rejection-letter event; relationships with classmates and others Not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet sought help for rejection-related problems before; no history of psychological counseling or treatment
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to concretely describe emotions and automatic thoughts; low tone, marked sense of shame; under guidance able to reflect and accept alternative explanations; fairly high cooperation; cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering, and mind reading present

basic_info.main_problem: After Receiving a rejection letter from a gifted program, feeling reputation damaged, continuously ruminating about this event and feeling Low mood.
basic_info.core_demands: Feeling overwhelmed by the disturbance of the rejection letter and the thought of 'reputation ruined', hoping to Learn to cope with and regulate these emotions and thoughts through counseling.
growth_experiences: Academic side has had positive experiences: excellent mathematics grades last semester, won a spelling competition last year. These achievements reinforce their self-schema of 'being seen as smart / maintaining high standards' and the sense of others' expectations.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough/not good enough.
My worth depends on others' evaluations of me.

special_situations.event: Received a rejection letter from a gifted program
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not admitted, it means I am not smart enough, reputation will be ruined.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Demanding oneself with perfect/all-or-nothing standards, repeatedly ruminating about failure afterwards and avoiding discussing with others to avoid shame.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My reputation is ruined; I am not smart enough.

special_situations.event: Thinking classmates or friends will know he has not yet been admitted (not yet receiving actual feedback from others)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others know about my failure, they will surely look down on me.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids communicating with friends (such as Cayden), keeps silent to avoid being evaluated.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am not good enough/not smart enough.

special_situations.event: In his mind, uses this rejection letter to judge his academic ability and 'smart' identity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One important failure can define my overall ability and worth.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging oneself by the standard of 'either admitted or not smart', labeling oneself with a single result.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not get in this time, then I am not smart.

special_situations.event: When recalling past achievements (such as math grades and spelling competitions), attention still stays only on this rejection
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Other achievements are not important, only this result shows my true level.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive evidence, continuously focusing on negative events to prove to oneself the belief of 'not good enough'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those grades do not count, this time is the key.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and seen as smart, maintaining a Good reputation
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated and humiliated, being looked down upon, losing sense of worth
defense_goal: Avoids exposing vulnerability and failure information to maintain self-image
Maintaining a controllable and perfect self-narrative through all-or-nothing standards

object_relations.self_representation: A self easily judged and possibly a failure
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges/others who look down on oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking of disclosing the rejection letter to his good friend Cayden or others, or when asked by others about the application result
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will look down on me, negating my ability (transference: Projecting inner Self-doubt onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding vaguely and evasively, such as 'nothing' 'do not want to talk', reducing self-disclosure, tone cautious, brief.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others affirm her past achievements and try to balance her view
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: This rejection letter is more important, other achievements are not enough to prove I am capable
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use rational Interpretation to emphasize the decisiveness of this result, using statements like 'this time is different/more important' to negate positive evidence, tone resolute but downcast.

manifestations: Fearing being looked down upon and unwilling to reveal the rejection letter to others (including best friend Cayden)
Imagines others as negative judges and chooses to bear the shame and frustration alone
Continuous Self-denial, weakening genuine connection and support with others
outcomes: Increased subjective sense of isolation, support system not yet activated
Decreased Learning drive, intensified doubts about self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Worrying about 'appearing weak', Suppressing expression of needs and emotions
Over-assessing risks before communicating with friends, long unwilling to start conversations

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Believing classmates and friends will look down on him, even without actual evidence
Uses 'others will evaluate negatively' as a reason to avoid seeking help and honesty

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Takes the standard 'must be admitted to count as smart / respectable' as the sole basis of evaluation
Defines overall self-worth by a single outcome

positive_force: Has stable social support (best friend Cayden), can obtain support when needed
Has past academic achievements (excellent mathematics results, won a spelling competition), possessing evidence of real ability
Able to clearly express emotions and thoughts, willing to seek help
Under guidance, able to conduct evidence examination and alternative thinking, with the potential to adjust cognitions
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mind reading, all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralization, and mental filtering are evident
Highly dependent on external evaluation (reputation / others' opinions) to determine self-worth
Avoids disclosure and seeking support, leading to subjective isolation and maintained emotions
Overemphasizing a single failure, weakening positive evidence, Reinforcing the failure narrative

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly ponders the rejection letter event and makes negative self-evaluations (rumination)
antecedent: Sees or thinks of cues related to the genius program and application
Recalling the scene of receiving the rejection letter when Being alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic cognition about reputation damage and the all-or-nothing belief that 'a single failure can define all ability'
target_behavior.function: In the short term, tries to gain a sense of control and explanation through rumination, but actually avoids direct emotional processing and help-seeking
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent Low mood, attention and Decreased drive, affecting Learning interest

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding disclosing rejection and seeking support from others (especially one's good friend Cayden)
antecedent: When thinking of telling friends or being asked by others about application results
Anticipatory worries before interacting with classmates/friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being looked down upon and shame, Projecting Self-denial as others' negative evaluations
target_behavior.function: Escapes possible negative evaluation and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Increased subjective sense of isolation, support system not yet activated, pain maintained

target_behavior.behavior: Verbal/cognitive judgment defining overall academic ability by a single rejection
antecedent: When academic identity or achievement topics come up
When comparing past achievements with current setbacks
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization, strong external-validation orientation
target_behavior.function: Providing a seemingly consistent Interpretation framework for current emotions and Self-doubt (Rationalization)
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, Decreased Learning motivation, further Reinforcing the negative self-schema
